$comment: Source of truth for the development log. docs/DEV-LOG.md is generated from this by `npm run devlog`; do not hand-edit the table there. Anything git can derive (commits, lines changed, files touched) is left out on purpose — only enter what git cannot know.

sessions.label: Phase 0 — scaffold
sessions.landed: Type model, seeded RNG, dice resolver, engine-isolation guard verified by deliberate violation. Four GDD ambiguities resolved.

defects.what: Dependencies two years stale; 5 advisories including a path traversal in @vitest/mocker

sessions.label: Phase 1a–1c
sessions.landed: Tuning constants. Labyrinth generation + ASCII map tool. Rewrite to 10x10 with difficulty contracts and the pit-free invariant; stone-grub retired. Wumpus scent AI, honest tells, hunt visualiser. Turn order corrected, metallic Heart tell. (Token figure covers session 3 as well — same conversation day.)

defects.what: 7.1% of seeds placed the Heart too deep to return from — unwinnable before the first action
68.7% of seeds forced the player across a hazard with no alternative route
Tier 4 Wumpus walked past a player it could smell, to guard the entrance
Player walked clean through the Wumpus — one catch check, made after the Wumpus moved
Fairness invariant mis-specified: 'never caught without warning' is not true, and should not be
Vertical doors drawn one column right of their rooms
Hunt map drew no hazards or creatures, so the tells had nothing to check against

sessions.label: Docs and hygiene
sessions.landed: GDD 2.17 information model. Phase 1 progress note. Remote branch hygiene; main pushed. Dev log and generator. Token usage is folded into session 2.

sessions.label: Phase 1d — creatures
sessions.landed: Creatures, encounters, taming bands, companion passives, SEND and world drift (src/engine/creatures.ts). GDD 2.9.1 written from scratch — it was referenced in three places and had never existed. scripts/tame.ts visualiser with a SWEEP aggregate mode. Room gained creatureHostile; a critically failed tame now permanently removes TAME from that creature's menu, and drift carries the hostility with the creature. Bloom spreading cut from within-run drift on Gautham's call — inside a visit the labyrinth only stirs, terrain is fixed. Wumpus start distance became a per-difficulty band in generate.ts, fixing a monster that could not reach the player in 83% of Drowsing and 63% of Stirring seeds. Nine invariant assertions mutation-checked. Findings 1 and 2 (SEND reachability and decoy strength) left untuned as design calls; the PM session decided both the same day.

defects.what: GDD 2.9.1 (world drift) did not exist — referenced by the turn order, the roadmap and a tuning comment, with nine words of spec anywhere
Turn order step 7 ran companion passives BEFORE world drift, so a grellhound reported hazards from a labyrinth that no longer existed
A brave companion is unobtainable at starting stats — P(critical-success tame) is 0% for every creature at INT 8, and 0% for the Quiet One at every stat. SEND fired 0 times in 150 runs
SEND's decoy out-smells the player for 1 turn while carrying the Heart, not the 2–3 the GDD promises; COMPANION.sendDecoyTurns = 3 was a number no value of sendScent could honour
Wumpus start distance had a floor and no ceiling — mean 11 rooms away on a 10x10 against tier reaches of 6–18, so it was unreachable in 83% of Drowsing and 63% of Stirring seeds

The tame sweep's adjacency metric undercounted: runs that ended in a catch broke before closestWumpus was updated, recording Infinity. Spotted because adjacency (40%) came out below the catch rate (47%), which is impossible
First hostility-travel test asserted the vacated room was calm, which fails legitimately when a second hostile creature moves into it during the same drift pass. The test was wrong, not the code

sessions.label: Phase 1e — resolve
sessions.landed: src/engine/resolve.ts — the reducer, implementing GDD 2.2.2's eight-step turn order including both catch checks. createRun, legalActions (deferring to encounterOptions, so the hostile gate has one implementation), replayRun and tellsFor alongside it. scripts/turn.ts visualiser with a SWEEP mode: it tags every event with its GDD step so out-of-order emission is visible on any turn you look at, splits 'caught' into which of the two catch checks fired, and re-checks replay determinism and JSON round-tripping on every run it prints. Both SEND fixes from the 1d findings implemented: TAME_OUTCOMES.strongSuccess.brave flipped to true, a natural-20 brave override added in resolve.ts (it cannot live in creatures.ts — resolveEncounter only ever receives the resolved band), and COMPANION.sendScent became a two-value lookup keyed off TAME_DC with sendDecoyTurns as two derived pairs. Brave companions went from 0/300 sweep runs to 10/300; SEND fires for the first time, though rarely. Three type changes: GameState.encounterRoomId, Player.statuses became a record carrying each effect's own clock, and GameEvent.roll gained an optional hazard field. tuning.ts gained ACTION_STAT, the hazard entry tables, PORTAL and REST. Six reducer invariants mutation-checked plus two against tuning.ts; all eight fail when broken.

defects.what: A hazard saving throw was emitted to the player as a MOVE roll — entering a snare room rolled INT vs DC 8 and reported 'roll move', telling the player something untrue about why they lost health. Breaks text parity, which is a claim about the event stream and nothing else

scripts/tame.ts Panel B hardcoded .criticalSuccess as P(brave), so it would have gone on printing 0% for the exact gate this session moved — a visualiser lying about the one thing it exists to watch, on the only day anyone would check

First version of the two-turn-tame test ran at stirring, where the Wumpus moves every other turn, so a one-turn fight and a two-turn tame could both show one move. The mutation (collapsing the step-5 loop to a single move) walked straight through it; rerun at hunting it fails as it should

First oil-schedule test netted the passive burn against skittish-companion upkeep and expected 1 where the answer was 3. The test was wrong, not the code — it now measures the burn events rather than the net delta

Claimed the determinism test was mutation-checked against an unsorted status iteration; it is not, because `confused` is the only status and a one-key object has no order to get wrong. Claim corrected in the test comment and re-verified against a real mutation (dropping the carried RNG position)

SEND's usage rate is still ~0.5% of runs after the fix. The band gate was the blocker and is gone, but the binding constraint is now encounter density (0.6 per run) — the same number already flagged as making the creature system 'one dilemma per run'

FORCE is in GDD 2.7 and has nothing in the world model to act on: Room.exits models a wall as a missing key, with no closed-door state. Not offered by legalActions, with a test asserting so, and flagged to the PM rather than invented
